Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning for the (Unstandardized) Contrast in Randomized ANCOVA From the Accuracy in Parameter Estimation (AIPE) Perspective

Source: R/ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity.Rd

Performs a sensitivity analysis when planning sample size from the Accuracy in Parameter Estimation (AIPE) Perspective for the (unstandardized) contrast in randomized ANCOVA design.

Usage

ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity(
  true_var_error_ancova = NULL,
  supposed_var_error_ancova = NULL,
  true_var_error_anova = NULL,
  supposed_var_error_anova = NULL,
  true_cor,
  supposed_cor = NULL,
  G = 10000,
  true_mean_Y,
  true_sd_Y,
  true_mean_X,
  true_sd_X,
  c_weights,
  width,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_var_error_ancova

population error variance of the ANCOVA model

supposed_var_error_ancova

the supposed error variance of the ANCOVA model, the planning value given to ss_aipe_c_ancova to choose the sample size

true_var_error_anova

population error variance of the ANOVA model (i.e., excluding the covariate)

supposed_var_error_anova

the supposed error variance of the ANOVA model (i.e., excluding the covariate), a planning value used with supposed_cor

true_cor

population correlation coefficient of the response and the covariate

supposed_cor

the supposed correlation coefficient of the response and the covariate, a planning value used with supposed_var_error_anova

G

number of generations (i.e., replications) of the simulation

true_mean_Y

vector that contains the response's population mean of each group

true_sd_Y

the population standard deviation of the response

true_mean_X

the population mean of the covariate

true_sd_X

the population standard deviation of the covariate

c_weights

the contrast weights

width

the desired full width of the obtained confidence interval

conf_level

the desired confidence interval coverage, (i.e., 1 - Type I error rate)

assurance

parameter to ensure that the obtained confidence interval width is narrower than the desired width with a specified degree of certainty (must be NULL or between zero and unity)

filename

an optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the realized contrast, its full and covariate-ignoring standard errors and their ratio, the interval width, and the three non-coverage indicators): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv")

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value summarizing the Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis across G replications. The term entries are: mean_contrast, median_contrast, sd_contrast (summaries of the realized unstandardized contrast); mean_ci_width, median_ci_width, sd_ci_width (summaries of the realized interval widths); pct_ci_less_width (proportion of intervals narrower than the planning target width); pct_ci_miss_low and pct_ci_miss_high (tail-specific empirical non-coverage of the population contrast); total_type_I_error (overall empirical non-coverage, the sum of the two tails); mean_se_ratio (mean ratio of the contrast standard error that ignores the covariate-imbalance term to the full ANCOVA standard error); and the input echoes n_per_group, total_N, true_contrast (the population contrast implied by true_mean_Y and c_weights), supposed_var_error_ancova (as supplied or as resolved from supposed_var_error_anova and supposed_cor), true_cor, width, conf_level, and assurance (present only when an assurance was supplied). The proportion rows are on the 0 to 1 scale, not percentages. The per-replication vectors (contrast, se_contrast, se_contrast_restricted, width_obs) are not returned; they are written to the comma separated file named by filename when one is supplied.

Details

The arguments true_mean_Y, true_mean_X, true_sd_Y, and true_sd_X are used to generate random data in the simulations for the sensitivity analysis. The value of true_sd_Y should be the same as the square root of true_var_error_anova.

So far this function is based on one-covariate randomized ANCOVA design only. The argument true_mean_X should be a single number, because it is assumed that the population mean of the covariate is equal across groups in randomized ANCOVA.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Lai, K., & Kelley, K. (2012). Accuracy in parameter estimation for ANCOVA and ANOVA contrasts: Sample size planning via narrow confidence intervals. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 65, 350–370. doi:10.1111/j.2044-8317.2011.02029.x

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapter 9.)

See also

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Monte Carlo sensitivity sweep; G is small here so the example runs quickly.
# Raise G (e.g., G = 1000 or more) for a stable sensitivity analysis.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity(true_var_error_ancova = 30,
                             supposed_var_error_ancova = 30,
                             true_cor = .2, true_mean_Y = c(10, 12, 15, 13),
                             true_mean_X = 2, true_sd_X = 1.3, true_sd_Y = 2,
                             c_weights = c(1, 0, -1, 0), width = 3, G = 25)
#>  term                      value 
#>  mean_contrast             -4.985
#>  median_contrast           -4.987
#>  sd_contrast               0.287 
#>  mean_ci_width             1.069 
#>  median_ci_width           1.061 
#>  sd_ci_width               0.038 
#>  pct_ci_less_width         1.000 
#>  pct_ci_miss_low           0.040 
#>  pct_ci_miss_high          0.040 
#>  total_type_I_error        0.080 
#>  mean_se_ratio             0.999 
#>  n_per_group               104   
#>  total_N                   416   
#>  true_contrast             -5    
#>  supposed_var_error_ancova 30    
#>  true_cor                  0.200 
#>  width                     3     
#>  conf_level                0.950 
#> 
#> Replications: 25
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity(true_var_error_anova = 36,
                             supposed_var_error_anova = 36,
                             true_cor = .2, supposed_cor = .2,
                             true_mean_Y = c(10, 12, 15, 13), true_mean_X = 2,
                             true_sd_X = 1.3, true_sd_Y = 6,
                             c_weights = c(1, 0, -1, 0), width = 3,
                             assurance = NULL, G = 25)
#>  term                      value 
#>  mean_contrast             -4.933
#>  median_contrast           -4.936
#>  sd_contrast               0.797 
#>  mean_ci_width             2.989 
#>  median_ci_width           2.991 
#>  sd_ci_width               0.065 
#>  pct_ci_less_width         0.600 
#>  pct_ci_miss_low           0.040 
#>  pct_ci_miss_high          0.000 
#>  total_type_I_error        0.040 
#>  mean_se_ratio             0.999 
#>  n_per_group               119   
#>  total_N                   476   
#>  true_contrast             -5    
#>  supposed_var_error_ancova 34.560
#>  true_cor                  0.200 
#>  width                     3

#> 
#> Replications: 25
#>
